## 2024-06-16 - Prevent credential leakage in proxy authorization errors and properly encode user inputs
**Vulnerability:** The proxy password was logged in plaintext when exceptions occurred (e.g., `requests` errors containing the proxy URL). It was also logged in plaintext during iterative processing logs. Furthermore, usernames and passwords were not URL-encoded when generating proxy connection strings, which could lead to malformed URLs.
**Learning:** Exception messages generated by networking libraries often mirror complete connection URIs containing credentials. The requests proxy standard is sensitive to special characters in auth fields and credentials must be appropriately percent-encoded via `urllib.parse.quote`. Logging raw configuration inputs is hazardous.
**Prevention:** Sanitize exception messages using regex before logging to strip passwords (e.g., replace with `***`). Implement helper formatting functions (like `mask_proxy`) specifically for logging configurations. Apply URL encoding (percent-encoding) for user/password sequences when manually constructing authentication strings.
